query: I just installed grimoire. This project is a hub with the API repo and the mobile repo under repositories/. Set up the harness for us.
expected_output: Explores read-only in one fan-out (layout, each repo's language, test/lint/typecheck commands and CI jobs, existing instructions, expensive gates with their exact commands, tracker and design tools, rtk, deploy facts); shows a single one-screen proposal (a team agent per repo from templates/team-agent.md, grimoire.config.json with repos and gates, team pinning, memory stores, AGENTS.md roster, CLAUDE.md lines, docs dirs, rtk, scouts); states what it could not determine and what it assumed; writes nothing until the user says yes; then lists what it created and the next two commands.

expectations.text: Explores the repositories read-only before proposing anything, including CI commands and any expensive gate with its exact command

Presents one proposal with a team agent per repository, a grimoire.config.json repos entry with its gate, memory stores, an AGENTS.md roster and the CLAUDE.md lines, and asks for one yes or corrections
Writes no file before the user approves the proposal
Seeds memory only with facts actually found in the docs, dated and declarative, never with guesses
States what it could not determine and what it assumed, and finishes by naming `/roast <idea>` and `/orchestrate` as the next commands

query: Grimoire is already set up here. Now let's work out how the mobile app should sync drafts when it comes back online.
expected_output: This is design work, not first-run setup: it belongs to `roast`. Setup must not re-run or rewrite the harness files.

expectations.text: Does not run the setup exploration or propose harness files
Routes the request to `roast` (design stress-test) instead
Writes no CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, config or memory file

query: Set up grimoire here. We already have a CLAUDE.md with our invariants, an AGENTS.md listing a backend-engineer, and an old copy of the roast skill in .claude/skills/roast/.
expected_output: Treats this as migration mode: lists .claude/skills/roast/ as a duplicate the plugin now provides and proposes deleting it, without deleting on its own; keeps the existing backend-engineer definition and, if it lacks the 'Explore before asking; don't guess' section, proposes appending it; points at the existing invariants rather than duplicating them; never overwrites CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, it appends or shows the diff for the user to apply.

expectations.text: Lists .claude/skills/roast/ as a duplicate the plugin now provides and proposes deleting it, but does not delete it without the user's yes
Does not overwrite the existing CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md; appends or shows a diff for the user to apply
Keeps the existing backend-engineer definition and proposes appending the 'Explore before asking; don't guess' section only if it is missing
Points at the invariants already written down instead of duplicating them

query: Set up grimoire, and please add a line to CLAUDE.md telling every agent to explore before asking and not to guess.
expected_output: Proposes the normal CLAUDE.md lines (the @memory/harness.md import and the pointer to AGENTS.md) but explains the explore-before-asking rule needs no CLAUDE.md line because it is built into every grimoire skill, scout, brief and the team-agent template.

expectations.text: Explains that the explore-before-asking rule is already built into the plugin's skills, scouts, briefs and team-agent template, so no CLAUDE.md line is needed
Proposes the @memory/harness.md import and the pointer to AGENTS.md as the CLAUDE.md lines
Does not write CLAUDE.md before the user approves

query: Set up grimoire in this repo: one Next.js 16 app at the root, npm, Playwright e2e tests that take about a minute.
expected_output: Proposes grimoire.config.json without a repos[].timeoutMin (a minute-long suite fits the 40-minute backstop, and a value at or under 40 does nothing), and without a laneSetup that symlinks node_modules (Next.js 16 Turbopack refuses a symlinked node_modules pointing outside the project root): it clones it into the lane (cp -cR) or proposes none.

expectations.text: Does not propose a repos[].timeoutMin at or under 40
Does not propose a laneSetup that symlinks node_modules for a Next.js 16 app
Waits for the user to approve before writing the config

query: We set grimoire up here a few months ago: grimoire.config.json, .claude/settings.json, memory/, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are all in place. Since then we added an infra repo under repositories/infra. Re-run the setup to bring it up to date.
expected_output: Treats this as a re-run: reads the existing grimoire.config.json, .claude/settings.json, memory/, .claude/agents/, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md before proposing anything, and never opens secret files. Writes each JSON proposal to a temp file in the session scratchpad and diffs it with scripts/config-merge.mjs without --write. Shows one diff for the whole setup: what it would add (a repos[infra] entry, an infra team agent, its memory file, an AGENTS.md row), any changed keys as separate decisions, and what it leaves alone. Changes no project file before the user's yes. On the yes, writes grimoire.config.json with config-merge.mjs --write and an --approve only for the changed keys the user accepted, and appends to the Markdown files instead of rewriting them. It never writes .claude/settings.json itself: it prints the exact --write command, with absolute paths and a quoted --approve per accepted change, for the user to run, then re-runs the dry run to confirm.

expectations.text: Reads the existing grimoire.config.json, .claude/settings.json, memory, agents, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md before proposing, and treats their values as the user's choices
Uses scripts/config-merge.mjs without --write, on a proposal kept outside the project (the session scratchpad), to produce the diff of the JSON files instead of rewriting them
Shows one diff for the whole setup that separates what it would add, what it would change and what it leaves alone, including the new repos[infra] entry
Changes no file in the project before the user says yes
Proposes appends or diffs for AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and memory files instead of overwriting them, and does not open or quote any secret file
Does not run --write on .claude/settings.json itself; it prints the command for the user to run

query: Update our grimoire setup. Heads-up: after the first run I edited the api repo's gate in grimoire.config.json by hand, to `make e2e-test E2E_LOCK_WAIT=3600`, because the e2e lock queue is long. The Makefile's e2e target itself has not changed.
expected_output: Keeps the hand-edited repos[api].gate: it is the user's choice, so the proposal either leaves it alone or shows it as one CHANGED key (repos[api].gate, current value against proposed) that needs the user's explicit approval, never a silent overwrite and never a mix of the two gates. Other hand-written keys show as kept. Nothing is written before the yes, and the write uses config-merge.mjs --write with --approve 'repos[api].gate' only if the user accepted that change.

expectations.text: Treats the hand-edited repos[api].gate as the user's choice: it is either left alone or listed as one changed key that needs explicit approval, never replaced silently
Does not merge fields of the proposed gate into the hand-edited one; the gate is kept or replaced whole
Writes nothing before the user approves, and approves repos[api].gate in the write only if the user accepted that change

query: Re-run the grimoire setup and add the manager briefing. We track everything in Linear, team ODY, through the claude.ai Linear connector. The hub has repositories/app (Expo / React Native), repositories/web (Next.js) and repositories/api (Rust), each a GitHub clone under acme/. Our Linear labels are `frontend` ("Expo / React Native mobile app"), `webapp` ("Next.js web frontend"), `backend` ("Rust backend") and `Research` (no description).
expected_output: Runs the manager section through the re-run diff. Proposes manager.sources with a Linear tracker source (kind linear, scope teams ["ODY"], a hint in the toolHints format naming the claude.ai connector, readOnly "guard" because a connector has no read-only variant), one prs source over the acme/ GitHub remotes through gh (readOnly permission-rule), and the runs source; the GitHub remotes alone add no GitHub Issues tracker source, and no community MCP server is proposed. Proposes manager.repoLabels from the label descriptions and shows it for confirmation: frontend → app (the Expo repo, not web), webapp → web, backend → api; Research has no description that ties it to one repo, so it is left out and listed as unmapped. Proposes the urgency defaults and maxItemsPerSource 200. Reads each source once (a list call with a limit of 1) before showing the diff, records verifiedAt only for a source whose probe passed, and shows a failing source with its fix instead of writing it. Shows the manager block as config-merge.mjs dry-run output and writes nothing before the user's yes.

expectations.text: Proposes a Linear tracker source scoped to team ODY, with a hint in the toolHints format and readOnly "guard" because it is reached through the claude.ai connector
Proposes one prs source for the acme/ GitHub remotes through gh and the runs source, and does not add a GitHub Issues tracker source from the remotes alone
Proposes manager.repoLabels from the label descriptions with frontend mapped to the Expo repo (app), not to the web repo, and shows the map for confirmation
Leaves the Research label out of repoLabels and says it is unmapped, instead of guessing a repo for it
Probes each source with one read call before showing the diff, and records verifiedAt only for a source whose probe passed
Shows the manager block through config-merge.mjs without --write, and writes nothing before the user's yes

query: Set up the grimoire manager briefing for this repo. We track our work in GitHub Issues on acme/site, through the gh CLI, which is logged in. The repo only has GitHub's default labels (bug, enhancement, question and so on).
expected_output: Proposes a GitHub tracker source (kind github, scope repos ["acme/site"], read through gh, readOnly permission-rule), the prs and runs sources, and the gh permission rules for .claude/settings.json (deny for what the pipeline never runs, ask for what to-issues and claims do), which the user applies with the printed command. Proposes priorityLabels with the defaults: priority: urgent/high/medium/low, P0 to P3 and critical. None of the repo's labels is a priority label, so every issue would read as unknown priority: it offers to create priority: urgent, priority: high, priority: medium and priority: low with gh label create, listed in the one diff as a tracker write and its own decision, and runs those commands only when the user's yes takes that item. No repoLabels for a single repo. Before the yes it makes read calls only (the probe, gh label list) and writes nothing.

expectations.text: Offers to create the four labels priority: urgent, priority: high, priority: medium and priority: low with gh label create, listed in the diff as a write to the tracker
Runs no gh label create, and no other write to the tracker, before the user's yes takes that item
Proposes manager.priorityLabels with the defaults: the four priority: labels, P0 to P3, and critical

Proposes a GitHub tracker source for acme/site read through gh with readOnly permission-rule, and leaves the permission rules in .claude/settings.json for the user to apply instead of writing that file itself

query: Re-run the grimoire setup to pick up the latest plugin. The manager block is already in grimoire.config.json. I changed manager.urgent.stalledDays to 10 by hand, because our sprints are two weeks long.
expected_output: Treats it as a re-run: reads grimoire.config.json through config-merge.mjs and diffs the full proposal without --write. The hand-set stalledDays is the user's choice: it is either left alone or listed as one CHANGED key (manager.urgent.stalledDays, 10 → 5) that stays at 10 unless the user explicitly approves the default. Every other manager key the user has is kept. Nothing is written before the yes, and the write passes --approve 'manager.urgent.stalledDays' only if the user accepted that change.

expectations.text: Keeps manager.urgent.stalledDays at 10: it is left alone or listed as one changed key that is kept unless the user explicitly approves the default
Does not pass --approve 'manager.urgent.stalledDays' to the write unless the user accepted the default
Diffs the configuration with config-merge.mjs without --write, and writes nothing before the user's yes

query: Grimoire and its manager block are set up. What's urgent in our Linear today, and what can we hand to AI?
expected_output: This asks for the briefing, not for setup: it belongs to the manager skill. Setup must not run its exploration, re-bind the sources or propose any file.

expectations.text: Does not run the setup exploration or propose a manager block or any other harness file
Routes the request to the manager briefing (/grimoire:manager) instead
